dish_name: Medaillons de Porc a la Moutarde
instructions: Trim any silver skin from the pork and cut it into rounds about 1 inch thick. Press each round down gently with your palm. Mince the garlic and chop 1 tbsp parsley.
Pat the pork dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams. Add half the pork in a single layer and cook for 3 minutes without moving it, until the underside is golden. Flip and cook the other side for 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and cook the rest the same way.
Turn the heat to medium-low. Add the remaining 1 tbsp butter and the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the broth, add the herbes de Provence and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble for 1 minute.
Stir in the cream and the Dijon. Simmer for 3 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

Return the pork and any juices from the plate to the pan. Simmer for 3 minutes. You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest round: a little blush of pink in the center is right, and the juices should run clear.
Take the pan off the heat and sprinkle the parsley over the top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the mustard sauce over the pork and serve.
method_notes: Salt & Lavender's creamy pork tenderloin medallions is the lead for the method and ratios: sear in butter and oil, garlic, broth and herbes de Provence, then cream, and finish in the sauce. Its flour is left out so it stays gluten-free. That page uses only half a teaspoon of Dijon, which is too little for a dish called a la moutarde, so the mustard follows the 1 tablespoon per half cup of cream used by Seasons & Suppers and The English Kitchen (2 tablespoons here).
